items.title: Microsoft Ignite 2026: New Sentinel Connectors Announcement
items.summary: Microsoft Sentinel helps organizations detect, investigate, and respond to threats across increasingly complex environments. As AI transforms security operations, bringing together the right data and context is more important than ever, giving human defenders and AI agents a more complete view of the environment to reason over and act on. These integrations bring signals from Microsoft and third-party technologies together across the security environment, unlocking richer context for investigations and helping power the new Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender , where human defenders and AI agents can reason across the environment with shared context. The connector ecosystem isn’t the only area seeing rapid growth. Microsoft Sentinel continues to add new capabilities, including Nested API support, Azure Blob support, and multi-account support, while AI-powered tools like the connector builder agent are making it easier than ever for developers to build integrations and bring more of their security data into Sentinel. At the same time, Unified Data Management , now in public preview, makes it easier for customers to manage their Microsoft Sentinel data, connectors, tables, and ingestion health in one place. For Microsoft Ignite 2026, we’re excited to showcase recent additions to this growing ecosystem and the partners making them possible. These new and enhanced connectors continue to broaden the security data available to customers, helping human defenders and AI agents gain the context they need across the technology estate. Airlock Digital for Microsoft Sentinel Airlock Digital helps prevent malware, ransomware, and unauthorized software with deny by default application control, allowing only trusted applications, scripts, and processes to run. Its Microsoft Sentinel push integration ingests execution history, browser extension control events, server administrative activity, and policy changes for monitoring and investigation. Included parsers map execution and audit events to Microsoft’s ASIM for analysis alongside other security signals. A customizable workbook supports investigation and monitoring, and teams can create analytics rules using the ingested data. NC Protect Data Connector for Microsoft Sentinel NC Protect Data Connector for Microsoft Sentin el from archTIS brings user activity and protection logs from NC Protect into Sentinel for centralized security analysis. The connector captures user activities and access-related events, while built-in workbooks support investigation and visualization of user behavior. By correlating NC Protect audit data with other security telemetry, the integration helps teams identify suspicious user activity, trigger alerts and response workflows, strengthen auditing, and monitor guest activity across SharePoint and Teams. blacklens.io for Microsoft Sentinel blacklens.io for Microsoft Sentinel brings external and internal attack-surface data, risk-prioritized vulnerabilities, darknet intelligence, and supply-chain risks into Microsoft Sentinel. The connector ingests exposed assets, compromised identities, stolen credentials and session cookies, typosquatting domains, and supplier activity on ransomware leak sites. The solution includes a data connector and analytics rule for creating Sentinel incidents, with configurable notification rules for alert severity and type. Findings are available in Log Analytics for correlation with existing Sentinel signals and can support custom analytics rules, workbooks, automation, and threat investigations. BloodHound Enterprise BloodHound Enterprise (BHE) helps organizations protect critical assets across modern hybrid environments by continuously uncovering identity attack paths and providing actionable remediation guidance. By integrating with Microsoft Sentinel, BHE delivers attack path data and identity security posture insights directly into Sentinel workflows. This helps security teams prioritize remediation efforts based on exposure to critical assets while enriching investigations into identity-based threats, including lateral movement and privilege escalation. Together, BHE and Microsoft Sentinel help security teams connect threat detection to underlying identity risk, speed investigations, and reduce opportunities for attackers. BlueVoyant Anthropic Claude Compliance BlueVoyant Anthropic Claude Compliance brings compliance activity from the Anthropic Claude Compliance API into Microsoft Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). The connector ingests Claude compliance events into Sentinel, giving security, risk, and audit teams centralized visibility into AI usage and related activity. By correlating these compliance signals with identity, endpoint, and other security telemetry, the integration supports threat hunting, investigation of policy violations and anomalous behavior, compliance monitoring, and repeatable audit workflows. Cato Networks for Microsoft Sentinel Cato Networks for Microsoft Sentinel brings security and network events from the Cato SASE Platform into Microsoft Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF) Push pattern. The connector pushes events into a dedicated Log Analytics table, making Cato activity available alongside other Sentinel data. By centralizing this telemetry in Sentinel, the integration enables security teams to incorporate Cato events into threat hunting, detection, and visualization workflows alongside broader security signals. Check Point EM ThreatCloud Intelligence Feed Connector for Microsoft Sentinel The Check Point EM ThreatCloud Intelligence Feed Connector brings threat intelligence from Check Point Exposure Management into Microsoft Sentinel. The connector ingests indicators of compromise (IoCs), including malicious IP addresses, domains, URLs, and file hashes, enriched with threat context such as confidence, severity, kill-chain stage, and campaign associations. An included playbook further enriches incident IoCs through ThreatCloud, helping security teams correlate intelligence with existing telemetry, accelerate triage and investigation, and reduce the manual effort required to maintain threat intelligence. Check Point Exposure Management Threat Intelligence IoC for Microsoft Sentinel Check Point Exposure Management Threat Intelligence IoC for Microsoft Sentinel brings threat intelligence from Check Point Infinity External Risk Management into Sentinel. The connector ingests malicious IP addresses, domains, URLs, and file hashes, enriched with context such as severity, confidence, and detected activity. By correlating these indicators of compromise (IoCs) with existing logs through analytics rules, hunting queries, and watchlists, the integration helps security teams reduce manual intelligence management, identify matches with external threats, and accelerate threat detection and investigation. Citrix SPA Sentinel App Citrix SPA Sentinel App brings Citrix Secure Private Access and Device Posture service events into Microsoft Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). The connector imports critical logs, policy outcomes, and user activity data, giving security teams greater visibility into application access and device posture activity. An included workbook supports visualization and analysis of Citrix data, helping SOC teams correlate activity with broader security telemetry, investigate security risks, support compliance monitoring, and strengthen threat hunting across their environment. ContraForce Events for Microsoft Sentinel ContraForce Events for Microsoft Sentinel brings security delivery and administrative activity from ContraForce workspaces into Microsoft Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). ContraForce is an Agentic Security Delivery Platform for service providers and security teams running triage, investigation, and response across Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel. The connector ingests incidents, privileged access changes, service account credential activity, and high-impact workspace actions. Three included analytics rules detect privileged access, credential, and high-impact workspace activity, helping teams monitor and investigate the platform supporting their security operations. Corelight for Microsoft Sentinel By transforming all network traffic into rich, comprehensive evidence, Corelight gives security teams using Microsoft Sentinel the visibility to understand exactly what is happening across their enterprise networks. In addition to native integration with Microsoft Sentinel, Corelight integrates with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Defender Vulnerability Management, and Entra ID to streamline investigations, accelerate responses, and remediate incidents quickly and easily. The Corelight App for Microsoft Sentinel includes intuitive dashboards, pre-defined workbooks , sample queries, and analytics rules that help make SOC teams more efficient and effective. CTM360 CTM360 brings external threat visibility into Microsoft Sentinel. The integration connects the CTM360 HackerView and CyberBlindspot platforms to Sentinel through REST APIs, so external attack surface and digital risk events flow straight into security operations workflows. HackerView surfaces externally exposed assets and security issues across your attack surface. CyberBlindspot adds organization-specific threat intelligence from surface, deep, and dark web monitoring. With these signals centralized in Sentinel, security teams can analyze external exposures alongside their broader telemetry and speed up detection, investigation, and response. Cyren CrowdStrike IOC Automation Cyren CrowdStrike IOC Automation connects Cyren IP reputation threat intelligence with Microsoft Sentinel and CrowdStrike Falcon to operationalize malicious IP indicators. An included Logic App playbook automatically retrieves known malicious IP addresses from Cyren and submits them to CrowdStrike Falcon as custom indicators of compromise (IOCs) for blocking and detection. Scheduled execution keeps the intelligence updated and automates the flow of Cyren IP reputation data into CrowdStrike Falcon for blocking and detection. Vaikora AI Agent Signals for Microsoft Sentinel Vaikora AI Agent Signals for Microsoft Sentinel brings behavioral security signals from AI agents into Sentinel for centralized monitoring and response. The connector ingests risk scores, anomaly and threat classifications, policy enforcement decisions, and audit data, including signals for prompt injection attempts and suspicious tool usage. Included analytics rules and a workbook help security teams detect behavioral anomalies, investigate policy violations, and incorporate AI agent risks into existing Sentinel incident workflows. Vaikora AI Agent Signals for SentinelOne Vaikora AI Agent Signals for SentinelOne brings high-risk behavioral security signals from Vaikora into SentinelOne as threat intelligence indicators of compromise (IOCs). The integration filters high-severity and anomalous AI agent activity and maps Vaikora risk scores to SentinelOne severity levels. The resulting IOCs are submitted to SentinelOne and expire after 90 days, enabling Vaikora security signals to be incorporated into SentinelOne endpoint protection workflows. DataBahn Agentic Data Control Plane for Microsoft Sentinel DataBahn’s agentic data control plane integrates with Microsoft Sentinel to provide our shared customers an AI-native data pipeline and orchestration platform that allows them to accelerate enterprise deployments. DataBahn’s pipeline standardizes onboarding and shaping across all data sources while providing operational visibility into data flow and health. Together, the collaboration focuses on reducing onboarding friction, improving normalization consistency, and enabling intentional routing, which helps security teams improve visibility, support threat detection, and streamline investigation and incident response workflows. Delinea Platform for Microsoft Sentinel Delinea Platform Sentinel Solution brings privileged access activity into Sentinel natively through the Content Hub, as a complete SOC package. The connector pulls audit events covering secrets access, authentication, session activity and configuration changes directly into Sentinel. Ready-made workbooks, analytics rules with baseline-driven detection, hunting queries and an automated response playbook let security teams detect bulk secret access, failed sign-in bursts and privilege escalation sooner, investigate without leaving Sentinel and answer auditors with a record of what happened and why it was allowed. Dynatrace Software Intelligence Platform with Microsoft Sentinel Dynatrace integrates bidirectionally with Microsoft Sentinel , bringing application attacks, runtime vulnerabilities, Dynatrace Intelligence problems, and audit logs into Sentinel, where analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks support detection, triage, and response. Sentinel can also send alerts to Dynatrace and enrich detected attacks with Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR insights. Bindplane by Dynatrace complements the integration by collecting and routing logs into Sentinel, including normalization to ASIM tables, giving SOC teams runtime and topology context for investigations. ExtraHop RevealX for Microsoft Sentinel ExtraHop RevealX for Microsoft Sentinel brings network detection and response (NDR) into Sentinel, giving your SOC visibility into threats that endpoint and log tools miss, including lateral movement and credential abuse hiding in encrypted east-west traffic. RevealX decrypts and analyzes network traffic at line rate, out of band with no impact on the network. The connector sends ExtraHop detections into Sentinel for dashboards, custom alerts, and investigation, so network context enriches your existing SOC workflows instead of sitting in a separate console. Fire Compass FireCompass Risks for Microsoft Sentinel brings validated external risk findings from the FireCompass platform into Microsoft Sentinel through the Codeless Connector Framework. The connector ingests risk data including severity, affected assets, assessment context, impact, and remediation guidance. By making validated exposures available in Sentinel, security teams can correlate external risks with endpoint and network telemetry, track remediation progress, and build analytics rules, workbooks, and hunting queries on top of FireCompass findings. Gambit Security Sentinel Solution Gambit brings resilience context into Microsoft Sentinel. It finds the resilience issues in your environment and syncs them to your Sentinel workspace daily, to help analysts see recovery risk before anything goes wrong. Sentinel correlates those issues with its detections. Your team can then prioritize the attacks most likely to disrupt critical operations: the ones hitting resources that aren’t ready to recover. Sentinel tells you what’s happening. Gambit tells you whether you can recover from it. Holm Security for Microsoft Sentinel Holm Security for Microsoft Sentinel brings asset data from the Holm Security platform into Sentinel via the Holm Security REST API. The connector ingests web and network assets into Microsoft Sentinel, including metadata such as IP addresses, hostnames, operating systems, tags, and vulnerability counts per asset. By incorporating this asset inventory alongside other security telemetry, the integration enables security teams to build dashboards, create custom alerts, and correlate asset information with other data in Microsoft Sentinel. Idira Endpoint Privilege Manager for Microsoft Sentinel The Idira® Endpoint Privilege Manager by Palo Alto Networks integration for Microsoft Sentinel pulls application events and policy audit activity into Microsoft Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework and the Idira Endpoint Privilege Manager REST API. Events land in a dedicated Log Analytics table, so security teams can analyze privilege activity alongside their other telemetry and build detections. IPinfo: IP geolocation & intelligence database IPinfo: IP geolocation & intelligence database brings contextual IP intelligence into Microsoft Sentinel to enrich security logs and investigations. The solution provides data such as IP geolocation, network ownership and routing, proxy and residential proxy detection, ASN information, and other IP classifications. By adding this context to IP addresses observed in Sentinel, the integration helps security teams better understand indicators of compromise, prioritize security events, strengthen threat detection and investigation, and inform network and access management decisions. Island Solution for Microsoft Sentinel Island Solution for Microsoft Sentinel brings user activity and administrative audit events from the Island Enterprise Browser into Microsoft Sentinel for centralized security monitoring. The solution automatically shares events from the Island Management Console with Sentinel and includes data connectors and workbooks for user activity and admin audit logs. By adding browser activity context to existing security telemetry, the integration helps security teams monitor and analyze user and administrative activity and investigate potential security issues. NetApp Ransomware Resilience for Microsoft Sentinel NetApp Ransomware Resilience detects and contains ransomware attacks on NetApp ONTAP workloads in real time, then enables fast, clean recovery. Its Microsoft Sentinel integration enriches alerts with data-layer context, including attack type, severity, user and IP, and affected cluster, volume, and SVM. The NetApp SOAR playbook can take actions on ONTAP such as trigger immutable snapshots, block suspicious users or IPs, and take compromised volumes offline. Together, these integrations extend the NetApp Platform’s ability to help security teams triage and respond to ransomware attacks, limit data loss, protect recovery points, and coordinate response across storage and security teams. NordStellar for Microsoft Sentinel NordLayer Intelligence by NordStellar for Microsoft Sentinel brings external threat and exposure findings into Sentinel through the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API. The integration provides findings including leaked credentials, breach exposures, malware and info-stealer infections, dark web activity, domain impersonation risks, and external attack surface vulnerabilities. By correlating these findings with other security telemetry in Sentinel, the solution helps teams investigate external threats, identify exposures affecting their organization, and automate triage and response through analytics rules and SOAR playbooks. Panorays for Microsoft Sentinel Panorays for Microsoft Sentinel brings third-party security findings from the Panorays platform into Sentinel through the Panorays API. The connector provides security teams with visibility into the security posture of vendors and supply-chain organizations, making third-party risk and vulnerability findings available alongside other security telemetry. By incorporating Panorays findings into Sentinel workflows, the integration helps SOC teams centrally monitor and investigate third-party risks and correlate them with internal security signals. USTA Account Takeover Prevention Sentinel Connector USTA Account Takeover Prevention Sentinel Connector brings compromised credential intelligence from the PRODAFT USTA Threat Intelligence platform into Microsoft Sentinel. The connector ingests alerts for exposed corporate credentials, enabling security teams to investigate potential account takeover risks within existing Sentinel workflows. Included analytics can identify newly compromised credentials and successful Microsoft Entra ID sign-ins involving known-compromised accounts, helping SOC teams operationalize external credential intelligence and prioritize investigation and response. USTA IoC Threat Stream for Sentinel USTA IoC Threat Stream for Sentinel brings curated indicators of compromise (IoCs) from the PRODAFT USTA Threat Stream into Microsoft Sentinel Threat Intelligence. The integration provides indicators including malicious URLs, phishing sites, and malware hashes derived from PRODAFT investigations. By making these indicators available for correlation with existing telemetry, hunting queries, and detection rules, the solution helps security teams identify connections to malicious infrastructure, investigate phishing and malware activity, and incorporate external threat intelligence into existing triage and response workflows. USTA Payment Card Fraud Intelligence Sentinel Connector USTA Payment Card Fraud Intelligence Sentinel Connector brings compromised payment card intelligence from the PRODAFT USTA Threat Intelligence platform into Microsoft Sentinel. The connector retrieves alerts associated with an organization’s payment card BIN ranges and makes them available within Sentinel for investigation. Included analytics identify newly exposed and non-expired compromised cards, helping security teams centralize payment fraud intelligence, prioritize potentially actionable exposures, and incorporate them into existing investigation and response workflows. Pulumi Cloud Audit Logs for Microsoft Sentinel Pulumi Cloud Audit Logs for Microsoft Sentinel brings audit logs from Pulumi, the infrastructure platform for humans and agents, into Microsoft Sentinel through the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). The connector ingests authentication events, organization membership changes, stack lifecycle operations, policy changes, and access token usage. It also includes three analytics rules that detect failed login attempts, stack deletions, and organization membership changes. Your security team can see what a human or agent did, when, and where across infrastructure as code, secrets, configuration, and policies, which helps speed up security and governance investigations. QCrypton PQC Scanner for Microsoft Sentinel QCrypton PQC Scanner for Microsoft Sentinel brings post-quantum cryptography readiness findings from Azure environments into Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). The connector provides visibility into cryptographic assets including Key Vault keys, TLS certificates and configurations, and Entra ID app registration certificates, with quantum posture ratings and risk scores. Included are six analytics rules, a workbook, and a notification playbook to help security teams identify vulnerable cryptographic assets and prioritize post-quantum migration planning. SailPoint for Microsoft Sentinel SailPoint for Microsoft Sentinel brings identity security telemetry from SailPoint Identity Security Cloud into Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). The solution streams audit and search events into Sentinel tables, where analysts can correlate identity activity with other security signals and query SailPoint APIs for additional identity and account context during incident triage. Automated playbooks can also remediate threats by revoking access or disabling compromised accounts, helping teams connect identity insight with investigation and response. SAP LogServ (RISE), S/4HANA Cloud private edition SAP LogServ (RISE), S/4HANA Cloud private edition extends Microsoft Sentinel security monitoring for SAP RISE environments with infrastructure, database, operating system, and network security logs managed by SAP Enterprise Cloud Services. Deployed alongside the Microsoft Sentinel Solution for SAP applications, it complements application-layer monitoring to provide visibility across the SAP stack and enable cross-layer threat detection and correlation. The solution supports near real-time log collection, built-in analytics and workbooks, ASIM-based security content, and correlation with signals from endpoints, Microsoft Entra ID, and other sources in Microsoft Sentinel. MailRisk data connector for Microsoft Sentinel MailRisk data connector for Microsoft Sentinel brings suspicious email data analyzed by users through Secure Practice MailRisk into Sentinel. The connector ingests enriched email metadata and risk assessment updates from the Secure Practice API, providing potential indicators of compromise identified from reported emails. By incorporating MailRisk data alongside other security telemetry, the integration helps security teams correlate suspicious email activity, search and investigate potential threats, and incorporate user-reported email intelligence into alerting and incident response workflows. SecurityScorecard Ratings for Microsoft Sentinel SecurityScorecard Ratings for Microsoft Sentinel provides cybersecurity posture ratings based on continuously monitored risk factors and threat intelligence. SecurityScorecard evaluates organizations using an A-F rating, helping security teams identify and track cybersecurity risks. The solution supports use cases including enterprise cyber risk management, third-party risk monitoring, executive reporting, and cyber due diligence. SIGNL4 - Mobile Alerting & Response for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender for Cloud SIGNL4 bridges the gap between security detection and human response with mobile-first alerting and incident management for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender for Cloud. Its two-way integrations allow security teams to acknowledge, escalate, and resolve incidents directly from their mobile devices, with updates automatically synchronized back to Sentinel. Critical Defender for Cloud findings trigger actionable response workflows, while persistent mobile notifications, automated escalations, and on-call scheduling ensure the right people are reached when it matters most. The result is faster incident response, clear accountability, and a fully auditable process - wherever responders are. SOC Prime Audit CCP SOC Prime Audit CCP brings SOC Prime Platform audit logs into Microsoft Sentinel for centralized security monitoring and analysis. The connector ingests platform activity including user actions, API calls, and administrative events, providing an audit trail across detection engineering processes. By correlating SOC Prime activity with other security signals in Sentinel, the integration helps security teams investigate platform activity, support compliance monitoring, and incorporate audit telemetry into broader threat detection and response workflows. SOCRadar Alerts Azure Sentinel Directional Solution SOCRadar Threat Intelligence for Microsoft Sentinel enriches security operations by bringing prioritized, context-rich alerts directly into Microsoft Sentinel. Covering SOCRadar’s Extended Threat Intelligence capabilities, including Brand Protection, External Attack Surface Management (ASM), Third-Party Findings, and other security modules, the integration helps organizations monitor external threats and manage investigations within their existing SOC workflows. Bidirectional synchronization also helps keep incident status, severity, and comments aligned between Microsoft Sentinel and SOCRadar. SpyCloud Enterprise Protection for Microsoft Sentinel SpyCloud Enterprise Protection for Microsoft Sentinel brings stolen identity data from infostealer malware, phishing attacks, and third-party breaches into Microsoft Sentinel, helping security teams uncover compromised identities, prioritize high-risk exposures, and accelerate remediation to prevent session hijacking and other targeted identity-based attacks. The solution includes a custom API connector, a Logic Apps playbook for ingesting data into Log Analytics, analytic rules that generate Sentinel incidents from breach and malware data, and additional Logic Apps playbooks for incident automation and enrichment. Tenable App for Microsoft Sentinel Tenable App for Microsoft Sentinel brings asset and vulnerability data from Tenable One Vulnerability Management into Sentinel for centralized security analysis. The integration combines Tenable cyber exposure insights with Sentinel’s collection, detection, and investigation capabilities, making vulnerability context available alongside other security telemetry. By incorporating asset and vulnerability findings into Sentinel workflows, the solution helps security teams correlate exposure data with security signals, investigate risks affecting vulnerable assets, and better prioritize remediation efforts. Uniqkey Security Events for Microsoft Sentinel Uniqkey Security Events for Microsoft Sentinel brings authentication, credential access and management, sharing, administrative activity, and platform threat detections into Microsoft Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). Included analytics rules identify scenarios such as sign-ins from unfamiliar IP addresses, excessive credential access, data exports, and security policy or privilege changes. A workbook visualizes activity and threat detections, helping security teams monitor password-management activity, investigate potential credential risks, and correlate findings with broader security telemetry. Utimaco Enterprise Secure Key Manager Utimaco Enterprise Secure Key Manager (ESKM) integrates with Microsoft Sentinel to provide centralized security monitoring and visibility into cryptographic key management activities through KMIP server logs. The solution enables organizations to monitor key operations, KMIP client activity, and authentication events, helping security teams identify suspicious behavior and investigate potential threats. Built-in analytics rules help detect brute-force authentication attempts, repeated permission-denied events, and key-destruction activity, while hunting queries and a dedicated workbook support deeper investigation of unusual users, source IPs, key retrieval patterns, and after-hours activity. valimail-sentinel-enforce Valimail enables organizations to see who sends email using your domain, protects against domain impersonation, and displays a verified logo in inboxes to increase brand trust. Our Microsoft Sentinel Connector brings Valimail Enforce event data directly into Sentinel, allowing security teams to incorporate our telemetry into unified SIEM workflows, monitor authentication and enforcement trends in real time, and build custom alerts and visualizations based on DMARC events. Once configured, Sentinel continuously ingests Valimail event logs, enriching your broader security intelligence and helping to improve your ability to detect and respond to threats across your environment. Varonis for Sentinel Solutions Varonis for Sentinel Solutions brings enriched, data-centric Varonis alerts into Microsoft Sentinel for triage, investigation, and remediation. Varonis insights are contextualized alongside other security events to provide a unified view of data risk. This allows security teams to view and close Varonis alerts directly within Sentinel, reducing the need to switch interfaces and supporting incident resolution with less manual effort Whisper for Sentinel Whisper for Sentinel enriches Microsoft Sentinel incidents and alerts with threat and infrastructure intelligence for IPs, domains, ASNs, and networks. The solution provides threat scores, supporting evidence, infrastructure relationships, and historical context directly within Sentinel. Included enrichment playbooks, analytics rules, hunting queries, and workbooks support investigation of threats including C2 communications, malicious infrastructure, suspicious domains, and BGP anomalies, while retained enrichment data can be queried and correlated with existing logs. Wiz for Microsoft Sentinel Wiz for Microsoft Sentinel brings Wiz Issues, Vulnerability Findings, and Audit logs into Microsoft Sentinel. Wiz identifies and prioritizes cloud security risks across areas including vulnerabilities, malware, internet exposure, identity, and data security in AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OCI, Alibaba, and Kubernetes environments. In addition to the solutions from our third-party partners, we are also excited to announce the following connectors published by the Microsoft Sentinel team: Agari Solution Akamai DDOS Protection Alibaba Cloud Networking Atlassian Organization Audit AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service AWS Elastic Load Balancing Cisco Cloud Security Cisco Meraki Events via REST API Crowdstrike Falcon Endpoint Protection Elastic Agent Solution Imperva WAF Cloud Solution Microsoft Copilot Microsoft Dragon Copilot Mulesoft CloudHub Alerts OpenAI Qualys VM Knowledgebase Rapid7 InsightVM CloudAPI SentinelOne TheHive Solution Trellix E npoint Security Trend Micro Cloud App Security VMware Workspace ONE Zoom Reports Building a more connected foundation for security operations The strength of the connector ecosystem reflects the work of Microsoft and our technology partners to support our shared customers. Together, we are helping organizations connect the technologies they rely on and bring more of their security data into a unified operational experience. For customers If you are a Microsoft Sentinel or ISOC customer, or considering adopting it, we want you to have the security connectors and integrations you need to get value from the platform. If an integration with an independent software vendor (ISV) is not yet available, or you have an issue with an existing solution, we have a dedicated team that may be able to assist by working with ISVs to build new or update existing connectors. If you have such a need, submit a request here . For software companies If you are a software development partner, the Microsoft Sentinel Codeless Connector Framework (CCF) provides a streamlined way to bring your product into the Microsoft Security ecosystem. Partners can also work directly with Microsoft for engineering guidance and support to build or improve a connector. Reach out to us via our intake form. Building a more connected foundation for security operations Our goal is simple: help customers protect their digital environments by giving human defenders and AI agents a more complete picture of risk. We’ll continue investing in connectors, partnerships, and integrated security experiences to help customers defend their organizations with greater visibility, context, and confidence. ContraForce Events for Microsoft Sentinel brings security delivery and administrative activity from ContraForce workspaces into Microsoft Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF). ContraForce is an Agentic Security Delivery Platform for service providers and security teams running triage, investigation, and response across Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel. The connector ingests incidents, privileged access changes, service account credential activity, and high-impact workspace actions. Three included analytics rules detect privileged access, credential, and high-impact workspace activity, helping teams monitor and investigate the platform supporting their security operations.

Corelight for Microsoft Sentinel

By transforming all network traffic into rich, comprehensive evidence, Corelight gives security teams using Microsoft Sentinel the visibility to understand exactly what is happening across their enterprise networks. In addition to native integration with Microsoft Sentinel, Corelight integrates with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Defender Vulnerability Management, and Entra ID to streamline investigations, accelerate responses, and remediate incidents quickly and easily. The Corelight App for Microsoft Sentinel includes intuitive dashboards, pre-defined workbooks , sample queries, and analytics rules that help make SOC teams more efficient and effective.

CTM360

CTM360 brings external threat visibility into Microsoft Sentinel. The integration connects the CTM360 HackerView and CyberBlindspot platforms to Sentinel through REST APIs, so external attack surface and digital risk events flow straight into security operations workflows. HackerView surfaces externally exposed assets and security issues across your attack surface. CyberBlindspot adds organization-specific threat intelligence from surface, deep, and dark web monitoring. With these signals centralized in Sentinel, security teams can analyze external exposures alongside their broader telemetry and speed up detection, investigation, and response. 

Cyren CrowdStrike IOC Automation

Cyren CrowdStrike IOC Automation connects Cyren IP reputation threat intelligence with Microsoft Sentinel and CrowdStrike Falcon to operationalize malicious IP indicators. An included Logic App playbook automatically retrieves known malicious IP addresses from Cyren and submits them to CrowdStrike Falcon as custom indicators of compromise (IOCs) for blocking and detection. Scheduled execution keeps the intelligence updated and automates the flow of Cyren IP reputation data into CrowdStrike Falcon for blocking and detection.

Vaikora AI Agent Signals for Microsoft Sentinel

Vaikora AI Agent Signals for Microsoft Sentinel brings behavioral security signals from AI agents into Sentinel for centralized monitoring and response. The connector ingests risk scores, anomaly and threat classifications, policy enforcement decisions, and audit data, including signals for prompt injection attempts and suspicious tool usage. Included analytics rules and a workbook help security teams detect behavioral anomalies, investigate policy violations, and incorporate AI agent risks into existing Sentinel incident workflows.  

Vaikora AI Agent Signals for SentinelOne

Vaikora AI Agent Signals for SentinelOne brings high-risk behavioral security signals from Vaikora into SentinelOne as threat intelligence indicators of compromise (IOCs). The integration filters high-severity and anomalous AI agent activity and maps Vaikora risk scores to SentinelOne severity levels. The resulting IOCs are submitted to SentinelOne and expire after 90 days, enabling Vaikora security signals to be incorporated into SentinelOne endpoint protection workflows.

 

DataBahn Agentic Data Control Plane for Microsoft Sentinel

DataBahn’s agentic data control plane integrates with Microsoft Sentinel to provide our shared customers an AI-native data pipeline and orchestration platform that allows them to accelerate enterprise deployments. DataBahn’s pipeline standardizes onboarding and shaping across all data sources while providing operational visibility into data flow and health. Together, the collaboration focuses on reducing onboarding friction, improving normalization consistency, and enabling intentional routing, which helps security teams improve visibility, support threat detection, and streamline investigation and incident response workflows. 

Delinea Platform for Microsoft Sentinel

Delinea Platform Sentinel Solution brings privileged access activity into Sentinel natively through the Content Hub, as a complete SOC package. The connector pulls audit events covering secrets access, authentication, session activity and configuration changes directly into Sentinel. Ready-made workbooks, analytics rules with baseline-driven detection, hunting queries and an automated response playbook let security teams detect bulk secret access, failed sign-in bursts and privilege escalation sooner, investigate without leaving Sentinel and answer auditors with a record of what happened and why it was allowed.

Dynatrace Software Intelligence Platform with Microsoft Sentinel

Dynatrace integrates bidirectionally with Microsoft Sentinel, bringing application attacks, runtime vulnerabilities, Dynatrace Intelligence problems, and audit logs into Sentinel, where analytics rules, workbooks, and playbooks support detection, triage, and response. Sentinel can also send alerts to Dynatrace and enrich detected attacks with Sentinel and Microsoft Defender XDR insights. Bindplane by Dynatrace complements the integration by collecting and routing logs into Sentinel, including normalization to ASIM tables, giving SOC teams runtime and topology context for investigations.

ExtraHop RevealX for Microsoft Sentinel

ExtraHop RevealX for Microsoft Sentinel brings network detection and response (NDR) into Sentinel, giving your SOC visibility into threats that endpoint and log tools miss, including lateral movement and credential abuse hiding in encrypted east-west traffic. RevealX decrypts and analyzes network traffic at line rate, out of band with no impact on the network. The connector sends ExtraHop detections into Sentinel for dashboards, custom alerts, and investigation, so network context enriches your existing SOC workflows instead of sitting in a separate console.

Fire Compass  

FireCompass Risks for Microsoft Sentinel brings validated external risk findings from the FireCompass platform into Microsoft Sentinel through the Codeless Connector Framework. The connector ingests risk data including severity, affected assets, assessment context, impact, and remediation guidance. By making validated exposures available in Sentinel, security teams can correlate external risks with endpoint and network telemetry, track remediation progress, and build analytics rules, workbooks, and hunting queries on top of FireCompass findings. 

Gambit Security Sentinel Solution

Gambit brings resilience context into Microsoft Sentinel. It finds the resilience issues in your environment and syncs them to your Sentinel workspace daily, to help analysts see recovery risk before anything goes wrong. Sentinel correlates those issues with its detections. Your team can then prioritize the attacks most likely to disrupt critical operations: the ones hitting resources that aren’t ready to recover. Sentinel tells you what’s happening. Gambit tells you whether you can recover from it. 

Holm Security for Microsoft Sentinel 

Holm Security for Microsoft Sentinel brings asset data from the Holm Security platform into Sentinel via the Holm Security REST API. The connector ingests web and network assets into Microsoft Sentinel, including metadata such as IP addresses, hostnames, operating systems, tags, and vulnerability counts per asset. By incorporating this asset inventory alongside other security telemetry, the integration enables security teams to build dashboards, create custom alerts, and correlate asset information with other data in Microsoft Sentinel. 

 

Idira Endpoint Privilege Manager for Microsoft Sentinel 

The Idira® Endpoint Privilege Manager by Palo Alto Networks integration for Microsoft Sentinel pulls application events and policy audit activity into Microsoft Sentinel using the Codeless Connector Framework and the Idira Endpoint Privilege Manager REST API. Events land in a dedicated Log Analytics table, so security teams can analyze privilege activity alongside their other telemetry and build detections. 

 

IPinfo: IP geolocation & intelligence database

IPinfo: IP geolocation & intelligence database brings contextual IP intelligence into Microsoft Sentinel to enrich security logs and investigations. The solution provides data such as IP geolocation, network ownership and routing, proxy and residential proxy detection, ASN information, and other IP classifications. By adding this context to IP addresses observed in Sentinel, the integration helps security teams better understand indicators of compromise, prioritize security events, strengthen threat detection and investigation, and inform network and access management decisions. 

 

Island Solution for Microsoft Sentinel

Island Solution for Microsoft Sentinel brings user activity and administrative audit events from the Island Enterprise Browser into Microsoft Sentinel for centralized security monitoring. The solution automatically shares events from the Island Management Console with Sentinel and includes data connectors and workbooks for user activity and admin audit logs. By adding browser activity context to existing security telemetry, the integration helps security teams monitor and analyze user and administrative activity and investigate potential security issues.

 

NetApp Ransomware Resilience for Microsoft Sentinel

NetApp Ransomware Resilience detects and contains ransomware attacks on NetApp ONTAP workloads in real time, then enables fast, clean recovery. Its Microsoft Sentinel integration enriches alerts with data-layer context, including attack type, severity, user and IP, and affected cluster, volume, and SVM. The NetApp SOAR playbook can take actions on ONTAP such as trigger immutable snapshots, block suspicious users or IPs, and take compromised volumes offline. Together, these integrations extend the NetApp Platform’s ability to help security teams triage and respond to ransomware attacks, limit data loss, protect recovery points, and coordinate response across storage and security teams. 

 

NordStellar for Microsoft Sentinel

NordLayer Intelligence by NordStellar for Microsoft Sentinel brings external threat and exposure findings into Sentinel through the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API. The integration provides findings including leaked credentials, breach exposures, malware and info-stealer infections, dark web activity, domain impersonation risks, and external attack surface vulnerabilities. By correlating these findings with other security telemetry in Sentinel, the solution helps teams investigate external threats, identify exposures affecting their organization, and automate triage and response through analytics rules and SOAR playbooks.

 

Panorays for Microsoft Sentinel

Panorays for Microsoft Sentinel brings third-party security findings from the Panorays platform into Sentinel through the Panorays API. The connector provides security teams with visibility into the security posture of vendors and supply-chain organizations, making third-party risk and vulnerability findings available alongside other security telemetry. By incorporating Panorays findings into Sentinel workflows, the integration helps SOC teams centrally monitor and investigate third-party risks and correlate them with internal security signals.

 

USTA Account Takeover Prevention Sentinel Connector

USTA Account Takeover Prevention Sentinel Connector brings compromised credential intelligence from the PRODAFT USTA Threat Intelligence platform into Microsoft Sentinel. The connector ingests alerts for exposed corporate credentials, enabling security teams to investigate potential account takeover risks within existing Sentinel workflows. Included analytics can identify newly compromised credentials and successful Microsoft Entra ID sign-ins involving known-compromised accounts, helping SOC teams operationalize external credential intelligence and prioritize investigation and response.

 

USTA IoC Threat Stream for Sentinel

USTA IoC Threat Stream for Sentinel brings curated indicators of compromise (IoCs) from the PRODAFT USTA Threat Stream into Microsoft Sentinel Threat Intelligence. The integration provides indicators including malicious URLs, phishing sites, and malware hashes derived from PRODAFT investigations. By making these indicators available for correlation with existing telemetry, hunting queries, and detection rules, the solution helps security teams identify connections to malicious infrastructure, investigate phishing and malware activity, and incorporate external threat intelligence into existing triage and response workflows.

 

USTA Payment Card Fraud Intelligence Sentinel Connector

USTA Payment Card Fraud Intelligence Sentinel Connector brings compromised payment card intelligence from the PRODAFT USTA Threat Intelligence platform into Microsoft Sentinel. The connector retrieves alerts associated with an organization’s payment card BIN ranges and makes them available within Sentinel for investigation. Included analytics identify newly exposed and non-expired compromised cards, helping security teams centralize payment fraud intelligence, prioritize potentially actionable exposures, and incorporate them into existing investigation and response workflows.

 

Pulumi Cloud Audit Logs for Microsoft Sentinel

The connector ingests authentication events, organization membership changes, stack lifecycle operations, policy changes, and access token usage. It also includes three analytics rules that detect failed login attempts, stack deletions, and organization membership changes. Your security team can see what a human or agent did, when, and where across infrastructure as code, secrets, configuration, and policies, which helps speed up security and governance investigations.  

 

QCrypton PQC Scanner for Microsoft Sentinel

The connector provides visibility into cryptographic assets including Key Vault keys, TLS certificates and configurations, and Entra ID app registration certificates, with quantum posture ratings and risk scores. Included are six analytics rules, a workbook, and a notification playbook to help security teams identify vulnerable cryptographic assets and prioritize post-quantum migration planning. 

 

SailPoint for Microsoft Sentinel

The solution streams audit and search events into Sentinel tables, where analysts can correlate identity activity with other security signals and query SailPoint APIs for additional identity and account context during incident triage. Automated playbooks can also remediate threats by revoking access or disabling compromised accounts, helping teams connect identity insight with investigation and response.

Deployed alongside the Microsoft Sentinel Solution for SAP applications, it complements application-layer monitoring to provide visibility across the SAP stack and enable cross-layer threat detection and correlation. The solution supports near real-time log collection, built-in analytics and workbooks, ASIM-based security content, and correlation with signals from endpoints, Microsoft Entra ID, and other sources in Microsoft Sentinel.   

 

MailRisk data connector for Microsoft Sentinel

The connector ingests enriched email metadata and risk assessment updates from the Secure Practice API, providing potential indicators of compromise identified from reported emails. By incorporating MailRisk data alongside other security telemetry, the integration helps security teams correlate suspicious email activity, search and investigate potential threats, and incorporate user-reported email intelligence into alerting and incident response workflows. 

SecurityScorecard Ratings for Microsoft Sentinel 

SecurityScorecard Ratings for Microsoft Sentinel provides cybersecurity posture ratings based on continuously monitored risk factors and threat intelligence. SecurityScorecard evaluates organizations using an A-F rating, helping security teams identify and track cybersecurity risks. The solution supports use cases including enterprise cyber risk management, third-party risk monitoring, executive reporting, and cyber due diligence.

Tenable App for Microsoft Sentinel

Uniqkey Security Events for Microsoft Sentinel

valimail-sentinel-enforce

Varonis insights are contextualized alongside other security events to provide a unified view of data risk. This allows security teams to view and close Varonis alerts directly within Sentinel, reducing the need to switch interfaces and supporting incident resolution with less manual effort

Whisper for Sentinel

Whisper for Sentinel enriches Microsoft Sentinel incidents and alerts with threat and infrastructure intelligence for IPs, domains, ASNs, and networks. The solution provides threat scores, supporting evidence, infrastructure relationships, and historical context directly within Sentinel. Included enrichment playbooks, analytics rules, hunting queries, and workbooks support investigation of threats including C2 communications, malicious infrastructure, suspicious domains, and BGP anomalies, while retained enrichment data can be queried and correlated with existing logs.

Wiz for Microsoft Sentinel  

Wiz for Microsoft Sentinel brings Wiz Issues, Vulnerability Findings, and Audit logs into Microsoft Sentinel. Wiz identifies and prioritizes cloud security risks across areas including vulnerabilities, malware, internet exposure, identity, and data security in AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OCI, Alibaba, and Kubernetes environments.

items.title: Ignite 2026: What’s new in endpoint security
items.summary: As more work happens in the browser, the browser has become a prime target for attackers. A fake CAPTCHA or a convincing error message persuades users to take an action that seems harmless, like running a command or approving a request. In these attacks, the user unknowingly carries the threat from the browser to the operating system. Once that happens, the attacker can install malware, steal credentials, or establish a foothold on the device. This sequence creates a practical challenge for defenders. Preventing breach at the time of execution is key, and at the same time security teams need confidence that protection is deployed, communicating, current, and functioning across all endpoints in the environment. At Microsoft Ignite 2026, Microsoft Defender is introducing protection designed to block some of the most prevalent browser-based attacks, and new capabilities to better and more easily manage the endpoint estate itself. Together, these updates connect two responsibilities that security teams often manage separately: stopping an attack when it becomes executable and continuously verifying that the protection layer is ready to respond. Protect against browser-based ClickFix attacks Today’s attacks often begin with a lure in the browser that leads to an attack on the endpoint. These attacks, called ClickFix attacks, accounted for 12.8% of all intrusions observed by Microsoft Defender between June 2025 and June 2026, with a 23x growth in volume seen between December 2025 and May 2026. Figure 1. Chart shows steep increase in unique devices per week running ClickFix attacks (source: 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report ) Today, ClickFix attacks attempt to evade protection by targeting many different execution surfaces (command terminals, Windows Run, Windows Explorer, Common File dialogs, etc), complicating detection and blocking of attacks. With the introduction of the new clipboard monitor (DefenderSessionHelper.exe) Microsoft Defender now detects malicious commands copied from web content before they can reach Windows execution surfaces. Remediation of detections (clearing the malicious content from the clipboard) will break the attack chain before the lure becomes execution. Remediation is currently rolling out to all devices running Defender Antivirus and is slated to complete by year’s end. Figure 2. Data copied by a malicious CAPTCHA is blocked by Defender For customers who have deployed Microsoft Defender, security teams will be able to see relevant detections in the Defender portal and can further investigate any relevant activity in advanced hunting. Figure 3. Alert timeline view in the Defender portal showing that Defender detected and blocked a ClickFix attack Figure 4. Detailed view of ClickFix attack alert Learn more about investigating alerts in the device timeline . Build more resilient endpoint security operations An endpoint can have the right policy on paper and still be exposed in practice. A device may be missing from the inventory, a sensor may have stopped communicating, an engine may be out of date, or an attack may reach an execution surface before the security team can respond. Across a large and varied estate, these conditions create an operational security problem as much as a detection problem. The new capabilities below strengthen that operational foundation. They help teams verify that protection is working, introduce changes safely, and manage devices through the full lifecycle. Monitor the health of every endpoint The new health dashboard in the Defender portal shows the health of your entire endpoint estate at a glance, across Defender components and platforms. It brings health signals into one place so security teams can quickly check that Defender is deployed, connected, up to date, and operating as expected across their endpoints. If they discover devices that need attention, they can move more quickly from visibility to troubleshooting. Figure 5. The dashboard shows data across four health categories The dashboard unifies four key views: Inventory : onboarding status and the top operating systems and platforms in the environment Communication : devices that are active, inactive or have impaired communication with the cloud service Antivirus service health : antivirus running mode and quick and full scan outcomes Update status : security intelligence, engine, and platform, each shown as up to date, out of date, or unknown Teams can select any section to understand what a status means, explore a detailed breakdown, and open relevant remediation guidance. They can also view and export a complete list of affected devices. Figure 6. A side panel shows a list of devices with communication issues With a shared view of endpoint health, teams can be more confident that protection is deployed and working across the estate. This feature will be rolling out to public preview over the next few weeks. Control how security changes are rolled out Resilient endpoint operations also depend on introducing change safely. Security teams need to move quickly on critical updates and new capabilities while protecting mission-critical systems from avoidable disruption. Customers have asked for greater control over how Defender changes are introduced across their environments. That’s why we’re introducing new safe deployment settings that provide visibility and control over the rollout of security updates and product capabilities across Windows and Linux devices. This new experience allows security teams to validate, manage, and adopt security changes: Roll out updates progressively: New safe deployment channels allow organizations to progressively roll out Defender platform and engine updates. Teams can now validate changes on a smaller set of devices before expanding to production environments. This helps protect mission-critical systems from unexpected disruption. Adopt new security capabilities when the organization is ready: Administrators can selectively enable individual public preview features based on readiness, risk tolerance, and business requirements. Together, these controls help teams keep protection current while managing operational risk. They make continuous security innovation safer, more predictable, and easier to manage at enterprise scale. Learn more about safe deployment controls. Offboard devices easily to close security gaps Resilient operations require control across the full device lifecycle, including retirement. Last year at Ignite, we introduced the Defender deployment tool, a lightweight tool that dynamically adapts to the operating system, delivering healthy endpoint security to a diverse estate. But just as critical as onboarding is offboarding, because attackers often try to use offboarding scripts to switch off defenses, e.g. in Octo Tempest-style intrusions. Devices need to be retired deliberately, in a controlled and traceable way. That’s why we are introducing a new offboarding experience that is embedded in the Defender deployment tool for Windows and Linux. Administrators can generate an offboarding key or download an offboarding package, set a custom expiration, use unique keys, and track the resulting package. With time-bounded artifacts and package traceability, it makes offboarding a defined administrative action. Once the device is retired, teams can return to the health and inventory views with greater confidence that the estate reflects the population they are responsible for protecting. Figure 7. The Defender deployment tool can be generated from the portal with an offboarding key Learn more about simplified offboarding. Extend coverage to shared mobile devices Resilient endpoint security must extend across every device and work model in the estate. Today, we’re expanding Defender to support shared Android and iOS devices. Shared mobile devices are commonly used by frontline workers across industries such as retail, healthcare, logistics, and manufacturing, with multiple workers sharing the same organization owned device across shifts. With Defender, protection remains persistent at the device, independent of the user signed in. Support includes onboarding, risk evaluation, threat protection, and collection of security telemetry. Devices must be configured in Microsoft Entra shared device mode and managed through Microsoft Intune. Learn more about Defender-supported platforms and devices. Collect custom data for Linux file data & Windows registry data Even with strong preventive controls, resilient operations depend on having the evidence required to investigate and respond. Custom data collection in Microsoft Defender lets teams define additional endpoint events directly from the Defender portal without deploying a separate collection agent. This enables use cases including investigating what ran inside a script, monitoring new server-side scripts on web servers, or hunting command and control (C2) communications. Today we are announcing expanded custom data available to Linux file telemetry, including file created, deleted, and renamed. This is helpful for teams that want to watch web folders and scheduled-job folders on Linux servers. We're also adding Windows registry events, including when keys are created, deleted, renamed or queried, and when values are set. These features will be available in Public Preview on December 9, 2026. Learn more about custom data collection. Endpoint resilience depends on prevention and operational control Endpoint attacks and endpoint operations converge on the same question: Is protection present, healthy, and able to act when an attack reaches the device? The new capabilities announced today ensure that organizations have the latest protections in place and provide security teams with insights and controls over managing security on their endpoints effectively. As these capabilities reach your tenant, review your estate health, and define whether a staged deployment path for Defender changes is right for your rollout strategy. See what's new in Microsoft Defender Join us November 17–20 in San Francisco or online for deep dives and practical labs to help you maximize your Microsoft Defender investments and to get more from the Microsoft capabilities you already use. With the introduction of the new clipboard monitor (DefenderSessionHelper.exe) Microsoft Defender now detects malicious commands copied from web content before they can reach Windows execution surfaces. Remediation of detections (clearing the malicious content from the clipboard) will break the attack chain before the lure becomes execution. Remediation is currently rolling out to all devices running Defender Antivirus and is slated to complete by year’s end.  

 

Figure 2. Data copied by a malicious CAPTCHA is blocked by Defender

For customers who have deployed Microsoft Defender, security teams will be able to see relevant detections in the Defender portal and can further investigate any relevant activity in advanced hunting.

Figure 3. Alert timeline view in the Defender portal showing that Defender detected and blocked a ClickFix attackFigure 4. Detailed view of ClickFix attack alert

Learn more about investigating alerts in the device timeline.

Build more resilient endpoint security operations

An endpoint can have the right policy on paper and still be exposed in practice. A device may be missing from the inventory, a sensor may have stopped communicating, an engine may be out of date, or an attack may reach an execution surface before the security team can respond. Across a large and varied estate, these conditions create an operational security problem as much as a detection problem.

The new capabilities below strengthen that operational foundation. They help teams verify that protection is working, introduce changes safely, and manage devices through the full lifecycle.

Monitor the health of every endpoint

The new health dashboard in the Defender portal shows the health of your entire endpoint estate at a glance, across Defender components and platforms. It brings health signals into one place so security teams can quickly check that Defender is deployed, connected, up to date, and operating as expected across their endpoints. If they discover devices that need attention, they can move more quickly from visibility to troubleshooting.

Figure 5. The dashboard shows data across four health categories

The dashboard unifies four key views:

  • Inventory: onboarding status and the top operating systems and platforms in the environment
  • Communication: devices that are active, inactive or have impaired communication with the cloud service
  • Antivirus service health: antivirus running mode and quick and full scan outcomes
  • Update status: security intelligence, engine, and platform, each shown as up to date, out of date, or unknown

Teams can select any section to understand what a status means, explore a detailed breakdown, and open relevant remediation guidance. They can also view and export a complete list of affected devices.

Figure 6. A side panel shows a list of devices with communication issues

With a shared view of endpoint health, teams can be more confident that protection is deployed and working across the estate. This feature will be rolling out to public preview over the next few weeks.

Control how security changes are rolled out

Resilient endpoint operations also depend on introducing change safely. Security teams need to move quickly on critical updates and new capabilities while protecting mission-critical systems from avoidable disruption.

Customers have asked for greater control over how Defender changes are introduced across their environments. That’s why we’re introducing new safe deployment settings that provide visibility and control over the rollout of security updates and product capabilities across Windows and Linux devices.

This new experience allows security teams to validate, manage, and adopt security changes:

  • Roll out updates progressively: New safe deployment channels allow organizations to progressively roll out Defender platform and engine updates. Teams can now validate changes on a smaller set of devices before expanding to production environments. This helps protect mission-critical systems from unexpected disruption.
  • Adopt new security capabilities when the organization is ready: Administrators can selectively enable individual public preview features based on readiness, risk tolerance, and business requirements.

Together, these controls help teams keep protection current while managing operational risk. They make continuous security innovation safer, more predictable, and easier to manage at enterprise scale.

Learn more about safe deployment controls. 

Offboard devices easily to close security gaps

Resilient operations require control across the full device lifecycle, including retirement. Last year at Ignite, we introduced the Defender deployment tool, a lightweight tool that dynamically adapts to the operating system, delivering healthy endpoint security to a diverse estate. But just as critical as onboarding is offboarding, because attackers often try to use offboarding scripts to switch off defenses, e.g. in Octo Tempest-style intrusions. Devices need to be retired deliberately, in a controlled and traceable way.

That’s why we are introducing a new offboarding experience that is embedded in the Defender deployment tool for Windows and Linux. Administrators can generate an offboarding key or download an offboarding package, set a custom expiration, use unique keys, and track the resulting package.

With time-bounded artifacts and package traceability, it makes offboarding a defined administrative action. Once the device is retired, teams can return to the health and inventory views with greater confidence that the estate reflects the population they are responsible for protecting.

Figure 7. The Defender deployment tool can be generated from the portal with an offboarding key

Learn more about simplified offboarding. 

Extend coverage to shared mobile devices

Resilient endpoint security must extend across every device and work model in the estate. Today, we’re expanding Defender to support shared Android and iOS devices.

Shared mobile devices are commonly used by frontline workers across industries such as retail, healthcare, logistics, and manufacturing, with multiple workers sharing the same organization owned device across shifts. With Defender, protection remains persistent at the device, independent of the user signed in.

Support includes onboarding, risk evaluation, threat protection, and collection of security telemetry. Devices must be configured in Microsoft Entra shared device mode and managed through Microsoft Intune.

Learn more about Defender-supported platforms and devices.

Collect custom data for Linux file data & Windows registry data

Even with strong preventive controls, resilient operations depend on having the evidence required to investigate and respond. Custom data collection in Microsoft Defender lets teams define additional endpoint events directly from the Defender portal without deploying a separate collection agent. This enables use cases including investigating what ran inside a script, monitoring new server-side scripts on web servers, or hunting command and control (C2) communications.

Today we are announcing expanded custom data available to Linux file telemetry, including file created, deleted, and renamed. This is helpful for teams that want to watch web folders and scheduled-job folders on Linux servers. We're also adding Windows registry events, including when keys are created, deleted, renamed or queried, and when values are set.

These features will be available in Public Preview on December 9, 2026.

Learn more about custom data collection.

Endpoint resilience depends on prevention and operational control

Endpoint attacks and endpoint operations converge on the same question: Is protection present, healthy, and able to act when an attack reaches the device?

The new capabilities announced today ensure that organizations have the latest protections in place and provide security teams with insights and controls over managing security on their endpoints effectively.

As these capabilities reach your tenant, review your estate health, and define whether a staged deployment path for Defender changes is right for your rollout strategy.

items.title: Vulnerability shielding: Protect the time before the patch
items.summary: AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery for defenders and attackers alike. An attacker can now turn a vulnerability into a working exploit within hours, but patching can’t keep pace. Our data shows that 38% of critical Patch Tuesday exposures remain unpatched for more than five days, and attackers operate in the gap between exposure and remediation. To keep up, organizations need protection that moves as fast as critical vulnerabilities are discovered, without forcing rushed patches or disrupting the business. That’s why today we’re excited to introduce vulnerability shielding in Microsoft Defender, in preview: Vulnerability shielding applies targeted, temporary protection to vulnerable systems in the gap between exposure and remediation, buying defenders time before they can apply a permanent patch. This AI-based capability reasons over the latest threat intelligence and each organization’s unique environment to choose the narrowest effective protection. Vulnerability shielding operates at two critical moments: Proactively limit exposure : The Risk Reduction Agent in Microsoft Perception as part of the Reduce exposure risk playbook creates a tailored plan for shielding vulnerabilities when patching is not immediately available or possible. Shields are time bound, reversible, choose the path of minimal business disruption, and retire automatically once the patch lands. Nothing is implemented without your approval. Protect during an active attack: When attack disruption in Microsoft Defender identifies an ongoing attack, it autonomously applies vulnerability shielding controls to exposed assets, cutting off new attack paths for adversaries and limiting the impact to your organization. Vulnerability shielding does not replace patching. Patching is the fix; shielding is designed to protect the interim risk. Autonomous protection enabled by a modern cyber stack Microsoft's cyber stack connects context, agentic reasoning, and native enforcement in a continuous loop. That integration enables vulnerability shielding to move from exposure insight to targeted protection at the speed an attack demands. Signals and context: Vulnerability shielding builds a deep, continuously updated exposure map of your environment across assets, identities, vulnerabilities, attack paths, and business context. This understanding helps determine where and how to disrupt potential attacks with the most effective protection, while preserving legitimate activity to minimize operational disruption. Actuators: Vulnerability shielding applies hardening policies tailored to each vulnerability and device, placed at the point where an attack can be cut off most effectively. It uses native enforcement controls in Microsoft Defender including reducing network reachability, restricting access paths, and tightening permissions . Agents: For preventive scenarios, green agents in Microsoft Perception can invoke vulnerability shielding when patching is not possible. They assess exposure and business impact, then recommend a coordinated plan that may combines patching, hardening, and temporary shielding. Reduce exposure. Reduce your exposure: The Risk Reduction Agent in Microsoft Perception recommends tailored vulnerability management plans. Figure 1: Reduce exposure risk playbook calling on the Risk Reduction Agent within Microsoft Perception, recommending a tailored shielding plan. Microsoft Perception helps teams act before vulnerabilities become paths to compromise. The Reduce exposure risk playbook uses the Risk Reduction Agent to prioritize risk based on exploitability, asset criticality, attack paths, patch readiness, and business impact. It then explains what matters and recommends the safest next step for security and IT teams to review. Vulnerability shielding is one of the capabilities the Risk Reduction Agent can invoke through the playbook. When a patch is available, the agent can coordinate patching through Microsoft Intune, with IT retaining control of deployment. When patching is not immediately possible e.g. because it could disrupt the business, the agent can recommend shielding. Shields apply targeted protection, buying teams time to work toward the permanent fix. The agent’s workflow is as follows: This transforms vulnerability management from a disconnected list of findings into a coordinated path from prioritization to protection. As part of public preview, the agent will provide vulnerability shielding for server-side RCE vulnerabilities, which make up 37% of vulnerabilities adversaries’ exploit. Once applied, the shield stays in place until the patch is fully deployed, then retires automatically. If you need to change course, you can roll it back with one click. Exclusions are managed through Microsoft Intune to keep critical devices and apps out of scope. You get room to remediate while staying in control of the business impact. Learn more about what else is new in Microsoft Perception . Disrupt attacks: Vulnerability shielding limits your blast radius Figure 2. Vulnerability shielding applied to a SQL server with a known public vulnerability in attack disruption Attack disruption in Microsoft Defender uses AI-powered analysis to detect and contain attacks at machine speed with over 99% confidence. It stops ransomware attacks in an average of 30 seconds. Every month Microsoft Defender disrupts about 68,000 attacks, protecting 580,000 devices from being encrypted. Utilizing the same confidence and technology, we are extending attack disruption to proactively shield vulnerabilities during ongoing attacks. On by default, attack disruption now automatically contains the exploited path and shields new routes the attacker could use - boxing them in with precise protections that reduce network reachability, restrict access paths, and tighten permissions . It acts autonomously, combining the use of the latest Threat Intelligence about vulnerabilities that are being actively exploited, as well as the unique context of an organization’s environment, to always seek the narrowest effective action and limit impact on an organization’s productivity. Crucially, the controls vulnerability shielding applies also analyze business context. Vulnerability shielding uses business context and baseline activity to understand who and what typically connects, it then applies precise network controls that block the exploit route while preserving established business traffic where possible. Security teams gain immediate protection, IT teams gain time to deploy the permanent fix safely, and finance users can keep working. Managing vulnerability shielding Shields are designed to be managed, not forgotten. Each one is temporary by design and retires once the patch is deployed, and every active shield is listed with the vulnerability it covers, the devices it applies to and why it was applied. You set the guardrails: exclude devices or apps that must never be touched, roll back any shield in one click, or turn shielding off. Before an attack, the Risk Reduction Agent simulates each shield plan against 90 days of real activity, so you see the expected impact before you approve. You can also extend shielding beyond published CVEs to vulnerabilities unique to your environment, such as in-house apps, legacy builds or AI-written code, and use your own detections to trigger the right shielding plan or attack disruption action. AI has made time the new attack surface but with vulnerability shielding organizations no longer have to choose between waiting for the patch and breaking the business. Microsoft Defender closes the exploit window in minutes, keeps you protected while you remediate, and gets out of the way when the patch lands. Vulnerability shielding is giving you protected time to patch. Eligible customers get: 90 days of retention up from 30 days for eligible Defender data. Lower-cost ingestion at $2.4 per GB to broaden visibility across Microsoft and non-Microsoft data through 500+ connectors. Search, review, and export these records to trace configuration changes to support compliance and governance. Learn more . Figure 1: Use audit search in Microsoft Defender to investigate changes to automation rules and generated playbooks. Microsoft Defender XDR Threat analytics

High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 Outage lures to target multiple industry sectors.

Advanced hunting queries

These sample queries search for campaign characteristics in Microsoft Defender XDR. Review the results in the context of your environment and adjust the indicators only after validation. The queries do not set a time range; use the advanced hunting time selector for the period you want to investigate.

Find messages by sender domain or subject pattern

This query searches for the observed sender-domain clusters and the randomized outage subject pattern.

let campaignDomains = dynamic([
    "moments-notice.com",
    "em4493.moments-notice.com",
    "newbooker.com",
    "em.newbooker.com"
]);
EmailEvents
| where SenderFromDomain in~ (campaignDomains)
    or Subject matches regex
        @"(?i)^(?:\[external\]\s*|\*external\*\s*)?outage\s*-\s*[a-z0-9]{6}$"
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
    SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, SenderDisplayName,
    Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc

This query identifies message URLs that contain the observed destination, click-tracking hosts, or tracking-pixel pattern, and joins the results to message metadata.

let campaignUrlParts = dynamic([
    "reallifeaccounting.com",
    "u113727626.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click",
    "url.newbooker.com/ls/click",
    "162.120.17.69:8080/t/v3."
]);
EmailUrlInfo
| where Url has_any (campaignUrlParts)
| project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain, UrlLocation
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents

        SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, SenderDisplayName,
        Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
    SenderFromDomain, SenderDisplayName, Subject, Url, UrlDomain,
    UrlLocation, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, NetworkMessageId
| order by Timestamp desc

let campaignUrlParts = dynamic([
    "reallifeaccounting.com",
    "u113727626.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click",
    "url.newbooker.com/ls/click",
    "162.120.17.69:8080/t/v3."
]);
UrlClickEvents
| where Url has_any (campaignUrlParts)
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ActionType, Workload,
    NetworkMessageId, IPAddress, IsClickedThrough, UrlChain
| order by Timestamp desc
